decisions.reason: As the flagship reusable citrus crate, its tooling is already paid for and it is cheap to keep, and harvest-crate adoption cycles are long, so the missing website evidence for 2020 to 2021 does not yet show that its value will not be realized.

The stackable crate line runs on existing tooling at low cost, but its absence from the website in 2020 to 2021 points to weaker prospects, so withdrawal is more likely than before while keeping the option still costs little.
Medium-duty rackable pallets serve steady pallet demand at low marginal cost, though their lack of visibility since 2019 lowers confidence in their value and raises the chance of rationalization.
The spill-retention pallet meets a niche regulatory need with stable demand and little holding cost, so the lack of recent website evidence alone is not enough to justify giving up the option.
The pallet with load retainers is a narrow specialty variant whose disappearance from view suggests limited uptake, but its low upkeep cost argues for keeping it for now rather than abandoning it.
